provider: Norwegian Geotechnical Institute (NGI) and Geoscience Australia; Zenodo hosted record
api_version: Zenodo record 16964551, v1 (published 2025-08-27); scientific PTHA model vintage 2017

request_contract.parameter_rules: Documentation-only paths for exactly Zenodo record 16964551 v1 and its two published filenames. The public file links use download=1; no caller-provided URL, host, path, record ID, filename, headers, search expression, pagination or other query values are permitted. Any future trusted probe must pin a single exact operation, explicitly validate redirects and DNS, refuse HTML/error bodies, enforce the stated original bytes and provider MD5, use a named User-Agent, and obtain a separate rights and execution review before it is enabled. No current network operation is authorized by this contract.

response_contract.format: Zenodo JSON record metadata; publisher README.txt text; semicolon-delimited original globalPTHA.txt (publisher-listed approx. 7.3 MB, MD5 d8dd8ad55fe89bd56b455e392387a99e). The publisher hash is a metadata declaration, not a computed original-byte receipt.
response_contract.scientific_semantics: Modelled 2017 global probabilistic earthquake-tsunami inundation/runup hazard, republished as Zenodo v1 in August 2025. rate_N is annual mean exceedance rate for height thresholds in centimetres; ariN is height in metres at a stated return period in years, not event IDs or event probabilities. Heights at 0.1 m and 20 m are censored boundaries; longitude may use 0-360 degrees; the README names ari500LZ while the displayed CSV header may use ari500ZL. This global screening/benchmark product is explicitly not recommended by its authors for local risk assessment, and is not an insured-loss or stochastic event catalogue.

operational_constraints.rate_limit_notes: Zenodo public developer documentation lists guest global limits of 60 requests/minute and 2000/hour, HTTP 429 on throttling, and recommends an identifiable User-Agent. These provider-wide limits are ceilings, not a license to harvest; the proposed future fixed probe would perform at most one small metadata or README GET, not bulk crawling.
operational_constraints.mutability_notes: Publisher record v1 is a fixed citation identity, but access headers and delivery links may change. Future original sample evidence must record UTC timestamp, exact URL/method and redirects, byte size, separately computed SHA-256, publisher-declared MD5 verification, media type, scientific parser result, and approved external storage identity. No original-byte hash or storage receipt was created in this review.

rights_and_policy.notes: Exact publisher original README.txt and Zenodo record 16964551 v1 independently display copyright NGI/Geoscience Australia 2017 and the CC BY 3.0 AU licence for globalPTHA.txt. The licence explicitly grants copying, adaptation and commercial use subject to attribution, licence link, preservation of relevant notices and change notice. This verifies the SOURCE-LICENCE legal ceiling for this identified original product, NOT current automated Zenodo download/service permission, service retention, user-specific third-party data rights, scientific adequacy, local-scale CAT modelling, or OpenCatastrophe raw/derived publication admission. Zenodo Terms of Use v1.3 additionally restrict platform use to non-military purposes and require following the uploader licence. Commercial automation remains unknown and the reviewed probe mode remains none until one exact bounded network operation and its service limits are separately cleared. Redistribution_status allowed describes only the upstream CC BY licence ceiling; no raw original files or derivatives are authorized for Git publication by this access contract.
